numerical_failure.observed_behavior: For descending sorts of complex numbers, complex numbers with only imaginary NaNs get sorted before those with only real NaNs, contradicting the intended NaN ordering semantics where real NaNs are the primary key.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: In descending sorts, complex numbers whose real part is NaN (primary key) should be ordered after those whose real part is not NaN; specifically, complex numbers with only imaginary NaNs should get sorted after those with only real NaNs in descending sorts.
trigger_conditions: Sorting complex numbers in descending order (less/greater comparison used by the sort comparator).
Comparator cases where exactly one side has a real part that is NaN and the other does not, while the “NaN-only” operand has NaNs only in its imaginary part.
Comparator logic using detection of NaNs in real parts (creal(a), creal(b)) and imaginary parts (cimag(a), cimag(b)).
oracle_clues: PR states: “complex numbers with only imaginary nans get sorted _before_ those with only real nans in descending sorts … they should be sorted _after_ (real nans are the primary key).”
PR body enumerates NaN/tie-breaking rules for the complex comparator with a primary key on the real parts and special tie-breaking when real parts are equal or both NaN.

C++ comparator change modifies real-part NaN detection by removing branches augmented with real-part NaN checks like “(ra == ra && rb != rb)” / “(ra != ra && rb == rb)” and changing the final return from “return ra != ra;” to “return rb != rb;”.

category_specific_evidence: Test constructs complex arrays containing real-imaginary NaNs: im_nans = arange + complex(0, np.nan), re_nans = complex(np.nan, 0) + 1j * arange, all_nans = np.full(100, complex(np.nan, np.nan), dtype=dtype).
Test computes immask = np.isnan(a.imag) to track imaginary NaNs for sorting behavior.

PR text states the bug concerns complex numbers with only imaginary NaNs vs only real NaNs in descending sorts: “complex numbers with only imaginary nans get sorted before those with only real nans in descending sorts, when… they should be sorted after (real nans are the primary key).”

PR body enumerates NaN handling/tie-breaking rules for the complex comparator: (1) if greater, push right only if the imaginary part is strictly NaN but the other is not; (2) if less, push right only if the other imaginary part is strictly NaN but this one is not; (3) if real parts are equal or both are NaN, break tie by float-like comparison of imaginary; (4) failing all (i.e., only one of the real parts is NaN), push right only if first is NaN.

Comparator change shows special-value NaN logic: previously included checks like “(ra == ra && rb != rb)” and “(ra != ra && rb == rb)” to detect NaN in real parts; later simplified by removing those extra NaN-augmented real comparisons and changing the final return from “return ra != ra;” to “return rb != rb;” (using the property that NaN != NaN).
